The Niger State Police Command has arrested a 32-year-old shop caretaker, Victor Peter, for allegedly breaking into five shops and stealing goods worth over N2m in Minna, the state capital. The suspect reportedly confessed to committing the crime alone, saying he stole the items to sell them and use the proceeds to play betting games. The police spokesperson, SP Wasiu Abiodun, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, adding that the suspect was arrested following a report of a series of shop burglaries around KFF Street, Gidan-Kwano, Minna. According to the statement, the incident was reported at the Kpakungu Divisional Police Headquarters on November 5, 2026, after about five shops were allegedly burgled around 8am that day. The stolen items included two power tanks, four native outfits, other clothes, four pairs of shoes, chargers, a power bank and a jambox, all valued at over N2m. Add us to your Preferred Sources Abiodun said police operatives launched an investigation into the incident and arrested Peter, who was the caretaker of the affected shops. “During interrogation, he confessed to the crime and stated that he perpetrated the crime alone on the same date at about 3.30am, when he stole the items from the shops. “He added that he moved the items to an unfinished building with the intention of disposing of the property and playing betting games. However, the exhibits were recovered from the building where he kept the items, and he has been charged to court for prosecution,” the statement partly read. The police spokesperson added that the recovered items would serve as exhibits in the prosecution of the suspect. The incident was reported at the Maje Divisional Police Headquarters on October 29, 2026, following which the suspect was arrested. Abiodun said Abdullahi confessed to the crime during interrogation and identified 22-year-old Zahradeen Aliyu as the alleged receiver of the stolen items. A search of Aliyu’s residence reportedly led to the recovery of three empty jerrycans used to store the diesel, housebreaking tools, including a bolt cutter, a 42-inch television and some clothes. The two suspects were subsequently charged and taken to court. The statement added that seven other suspects were nabbed over alleged thuggery and political violence during campaign activities in the state. Abiodun said six suspects were arrested by operatives of the Anti-Thuggery Unit at the Trade Fair Complex, Shango, on Thursday, while allegedly engaging in thuggery during a political campaign. The suspects were reportedly found with two cutlasses, four knives, scissors and other dangerous weapons. Similarly, another suspected thug, identified as Anasho, was arrested around Tunga on Friday for allegedly attacking a political campaign team and damaging its vehicles, banners and other materials.
